title: Picking, letting go of and cutting a clip while a long edit plays each finish within one frame
goal: On the 6 minute reference edit, clicking a clip, clicking away, and cutting or trimming the clip you have picked still hold the main thread for 15 to 33 ms, two frames where the goal is one. Make each of them, and moving a clip, adding a transition and changing a title, finish within one frame (16 ms) while the edit plays.
notes: Carried from a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed (28 passes, closed 2026-11-23 per its triage). Measure with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh (short form, ~2 min) and Scripts/perf/pass-profile.sh (PassSampler, edits-only walks; Instruments refuses without developer mode). Where the time is (pass 25 to 28): a landing pass has a floor of about 15-17 ms whatever lands: dock stack layout ~4.4, SwiftUI graph ~3.8, accessibility focus ~3.0 (AccessibilityNode.updateFocus -> ViewRendererHost.focusResponder walking every responder; SwiftUI accessibility is switched on in the probe by another process, so a person with any accessibility client sees it too), title bar drag regions ~1.3 (-[NSWindow _resetDragMargins] asks the hosting view acceptsFirstResponder, which walks every focusable control). A pick from nothing is ~30 passes over 0.7 s, one section or row set each. Leads not tried: fewer AppKit-backed controls in the panel (TextField and Picker as NSView, ~170 in the window) so the focus walk shrinks; land only the sections in sight during play and the rest after play stops; keep the clip sections built and hidden across unpick (13.5 ms of unpick is SwiftUI graph teardown). Tried and reverted: a Layout cache for PanelFieldRowLayout (worse), caching control minimums (no gain). Related panel-cost tasks: folding-a-section-that-lets-the-panel-fit-again, leaving-preview-slides-back-without-a-hitch.
acceptance: Closed windows give their memory back again: closed-windows-give-their-memory-back-walk passes (at most 1 editor alive after 12 pictures are opened and closed; it reads 13 since 221074d5f and 11c86b116), found and fixed first, before any further speed pass

Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh on the 6 minute edit reads a longest pass of 16 ms or less for pick, pick from nothing, unpick, blade picked, trim picked and undo picked, worst of three runs (2026-11-23: 29, 33, 30, 19, 15, 15 ms)
The speed walk also times moving a clip, adding a transition at a cut and changing a title while it plays, and each reads 16 ms or less

The panel still shows every section of the picked clip once play stops, and the walks that pick clips while playing stay green (cutting-while-playing-keeps-playing-walk, the-panel-catches-up-when-play-stops-walk)
Speed walk baseline rewritten with --baseline after the fix, and each fix logged with its before and after number

A clip picked while a video plays shows at least its Properties header and the clip's name in the panel in the click's own frame, so the pick visibly lands; only the sections below it may wait for play to stop (today only Time shows: queue/audits/2026-11-23-panel-waits-for-play-1.png). Pictured in the audit

Lead for pass 2: since the panel is the whole excess and is spread over every section, the one lever that clears 16 ms is the panel not re-running at the moment of a pick while it plays (hold what it shows and catch up when play stops or the pointer comes into the panel, as it already holds with nothing picked). Second lever: the window floor of ~13 ms per landing pass (layout, a11y focus walk over ~470 views, title bar drag regions), e.g. the 98 anchor views.

Pass 2 tried and ruled out (all as throwaway experiments in /tmp, nothing landed): freezing the panel by moving it into its own NSHostingView. Skipping the host's layout() does not stop bodies (SwiftUI flushes them from a run-loop observer); hiding it does not either; only taking it out of the window stops updates, and a picture of it to show meanwhile is not possible (cacheDisplay drops SwiftUI text and controls, 7 ms). So a full freeze would blank the panel during play.

Not reached (acceptance 1): pick from nothing 22.8 (first passes: clip bars + panel's own pass with Time re-running for the pick), pick 17.5, blade picked 16.6 ms worst of 3. Lead for pass 3: (a) the case the speed walk does not time, a pick while playing with the whole panel already built (picked then played), still re-runs every section in one ~26 ms pass: add it to the speed walk; (b) holding the pick for the panel needs the panel's reads of selectedLayerID to be told apart from everyone else's; the existing static-flag pattern (readingALatePass) only covers the body that sets it, so it needs either every section view wrapped or the sections given the subject explicitly; (c) the first pass of a pick from nothing is clip bars (3) + inspectorPanel (3) + Time (2): Time re-running for a new clip while playing could hold too (PanelPlayhead.clipInHand already holds with nothing picked).

Pass 2: panel pieces wait for play to stop (11c86b116): unpick, trim and undo picked now within a frame (12.8, 12.1, 13.0); pick 17.5, pick from nothing 22.8, blade picked 16.6 still over 16. Leads for pass 3 in the log.

Design review 2026-11-24, judged from queue/audits/2026-11-23-panel-waits-for-play-1.png: a clip picked while it plays leaves the panel showing only TIME (Speed, Sound, Fades). There is no Properties header and no clip name, so nothing in the panel says which clip is picked or that the click landed. Rule bent: UX-PATTERNS section 2, the panel shows what is picked. Premiere's Effect Controls names the clip at once during play. Keeping the header and the name up during play is cheap (one row), so it should not cost the frame.

Suggestion from triage 2026-11-24 (not a requirement): have the speed walk read the live editor count at the end of each run, so a speed pass that holds memory is caught by the walk it already runs, not 11 hours later by a rotating check.
